correctness.rationale: The free space on weighted graph vertices is isometric to weighted ell_1(E)/ker(partial) because the dual potential constraints are precisely edgewise Lipschitz inequalities. On a cactus, edge-disjoint cycles generate a direct-support kernel, and each spanning tree omits exactly one edge r_C per cycle. The quotient-map identity ||P||=max_e ||Pq(e)||/w_e reduces each suppressed tree basis projection to its images on generating edges. The omitted-edge image has norm inf_t[W_C(S)|1-t|+(L_C-W_C(S))|t|]=min(W_C(S),L_C-W_C(S)); selected basis edges and idempotence supply the 1 term. For unit weights each prefix count runs 0..|C|-1, giving max_C floor(|C|/2), independent of tree/ordering and monotonicity iff all cycles are triangles or absent. This also handles bridges and overlong presentation edges without assuming their direct metric costs.
